# reharness

> A self-improving agent harness: bounded recursive self-improvement (RSI) in which an LLM agent's own model revises the harness the agent runs in — tools, hooks, skills, prompts — from the agent's own returned runs, and proves each change with a live run before adoption. Measured on AutomationBench with Claude Opus 5.5.

Key facts:
- A Revision Session reads the agent's own returned run (no score, no expected value), edits a copy of the Harness Package, and proves the change with a Live Probe: the candidate runs the same request for real.
- Per-Task Adoption: only a probe that comes back accepted is adopted, and only for that task; an accepted task opens no session and is never revised.
- The session is never shown an answer: at most accepted/returned per attempt and which check failed (its kind and object).
- A Frozen Core the session cannot touch: the host-side scorer, the feedback tier, the package contract (no answer in the package), the bounds.
- Results: Claude Opus 5.5 scores 42.47% on the AutomationBench leaderboard; with reharness, on the benchmark's held-out finance tasks, 68% at steady state; across sealed finals up to +13 points over the same model without it, no passing task lost.
